title: Their halt at the meeting of Ganga and Sarayu
introduction: Rama and Lakshmana proceeding with Vishvamitra sojourn in a hermitage at a place where River Ganga and River Sarayu are confluent. Once god Shiva with his third eye burnt down the physical entity of Manmatha, the Love-god, at this place.
closing: At the rising of the sun as well as at noon certain observances, invocations, and prayers were prescribed which might under no circumstances be omitted. One of these observances was the recitation of the sAvitri, [Gayatri, so to say,] a Vedic hymn to the Sun of wonderful beauty - Gorresio.

Rama and Lakshmana meditated upon Gayatri hymn as there is no hymn superior to it; na gāyatryāḥ param japyam and this is also the usual hymn for water oblation at dawn or dusk: sandhyā vandana . sandhyā is the time between the day and night when the stars or the sun are not visible. aho rātrasya yaḥ sandhiḥ sūryanakṣatravarjitaḥ Then this hymn is to be meditated placing her in ones own heart or amid the solar system. gāyatrīm samsmaret dhīmān hṛdi vā sūryamaṇḍale.
इति वाल्मीकिरामायणे आदिकाव्ये बालकाण्डे त्रयोविंशः सर्गः ||
Thus, this is the 23rd chapter in Bala Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
प्रभातायां तु शर्वर्यां विश्वामित्रो महामुनिः |
अभ्यभाषत काकुत्स्थौ शयानौ पर्णसंस्तरे
verses.iast:
prabhātāyām tu śarvaryām viśvāmitro mahāmuniḥ |
abhyabhāṣata kākutsthau śayānau parṇa saṃstare
verses.translation: At dawn after that night the great saint Vishvamitra spoke to the legatees of Kakutstha, Rama and Lakshmana, those that are sleeping on a grass bed.

glosses.meaning: to the legatees of Kakutstha - Rama and Lakshmana
on the grass, bed, sleeping on

verses.devanagari:
कौसल्या सुप्रजा राम पूर्वा संध्या प्रवर्तते |
उत्तिष्ठ नरशार्दूल कर्तव्यं दैवमाह्निकम्
verses.iast:
kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā sandhyā pravartate |
uttiṣṭha nara śārdūla kartavyam daivamāhnikam
verses.translation: "Fortunate is Kausalya to beget you as her son Rama... get up oh, tigerly-man, eastern aurora is emerging, daytime tasks towards gods are to be performed."
notes: This is another celebrated verse chanted even today. So far Rama is a dear prince to his parents. But here, no less than Sage Vishvamitra said to have deified Rama in asking him to 'get up' from divine trance to undertake the human duties to eliminate evil, like the dawn of the sun eliminating the evil darkness. In other ancient manuscripts the same verse obtains as:

This early morning 'awakening' of Vishnu or his incarnates from divine trance is a common practice in Vaishnavaite tradition, and is followed even today, called suprabhāta seva , morning service to wake up.
For kausalyā su prajā rāma Griffith says: 'High fate is hers who calls thee son: / Arise, 'tis break of day /. And Gita Press has it as: Kausalya is blessed with a worthy son [in you.]

glosses.meaning: Kausalya, the lucky, begetter [Kausalya is fortunate because she begot you, such as you are]

verses.devanagari:
तस्यर्षेः परमोदारं वचः श्रुत्वा नरोत्तमौ |
स्नात्वा कृतोदकौ वीरौ जेपतुः परमं जपम्
verses.iast:
tasya ṛṣeḥ parama udāram vacaḥ śrutvā nṛpa narottamau |
snātvā kṛta udakau vīrau jepatuḥ paramam japam
verses.translation: On hearing the benign words of the sage those valorous and best ones among men got up, bathed, and on offering water oblation they mediated upon the supreme hymn, namely Gayatri.

verses.devanagari:
कृताह्निकौ महावीर्यौ विश्वामित्रं तपोधनम् |
अभिवाद्यातिसंहृष्टौ गमनायाभितस्थतुः
verses.iast:
kṛta āhnikau mahāvīryau viśvāmitram tapodhanam |
abhivādya ati saṃhṛṣṭau gamanāya abhitasthatuḥ
verses.translation: On performing their dawn time duties those two stalwarts, Rama and Lakshmana, enthusiastically presented themselves before the ascetically rich sage Vishvamitra for further journey, duly venerating him.

glosses.meaning: to Vishvamitra, whose ascesis, is his wealth
to travel, they presented themselves [before the sage.]

verses.devanagari:
तौ प्रयान्तौ महावीर्यौ दिव्यां त्रिपथगां नदीम् |
ददृशाते ततस्तत्र सरय्वाः संगमे शुभे
verses.iast:
tau prayāntau mahāvīryau divyam tripathagām nadīm |
dadṛśā te tataḥ tatra sarayvāḥ saṅgame śubhe
verses.translation: Then on travelling some more distance those two great valiant ones, there they have seen the divine river that courses in three ways, namely Ganga, at the auspicious confluence of River Sarayu.
notes: River Ganga follows three courses, firstly in heavens, second on earth, and third into nether worlds. These episodes on the descent of Ganga to earth are narrated in the later part of this book, Bala Kanda.

verses.devanagari:
तत्राश्रमपदं पुण्यं ऋषीणां भावितात्मनाम् |
बहुवर्षसहस्राणि तप्यतां परमं तपः
verses.iast:
tatra āśrama padam puṇyam ṛṣīṇām bhāviata ātmānām |
bahu varṣa sahasrāṇi tapyatām paramam tapaḥ
verses.translation: There they have seen the merited hermitage of sages with contemplative souls, and who are practising supreme ascesis for many thousand years.

verses.devanagari:
तं दृष्ट्वा परमप्रीतौ राघवौ पुण्यमाश्रमम् |
ऊचतुस्तं महात्मानं विश्वामित्रमिदं वचः
verses.iast:
tam dṛṣṭvā parama prītau rāghavau puṇyam āśramam |
ūcatuḥ tam mahātmānam viśvāmitram idam vacaḥ
verses.translation: On seeing that merited hermitage Rama and Lakshmana are highly pleased and said this word to that great-soul Sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: to him, Vishvamitra, this, word uchatuH = said.

verses.devanagari:
कस्यायमाश्रमः पुण्यः को न्वस्मिन्वसते पुमान् |
भगवन् श्रोतुमिच्छावः परं कौतूहलं हि नौ
verses.iast:
kasya ayam āśramaḥ puṇyaḥ ko nu asmin vasate pumān |
bhagavan śrotum icchāvaḥ param kautūhalam hi nau
verses.translation: "Whose hermitage is this merited one? Indeed who is the celebrity that lives therein? Oh, godly sage, we are interested to listen, and we are truly inquisitive about it." Thus they asked.

glosses.meaning: this, merited, hermitage, whose is it
in this, who, indeed, celebrity, dwells

verses.devanagari:
तयोस्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा प्रहस्य मुनिपुंगवः |
अब्रवीच्छ्रूयतां राम कस्यायं पूर्व आश्रमः
verses.iast:
tayoḥ tad vacanam śrutvā prahasya munipuṅgavaḥ |
abravīt śrUyatām rāma yasya ayam pūrva āśramaḥ
verses.translation: On hearing their words the eminent sage Viswamitra said smilingly, " whose hermitage is this in earlier times that may be listened." Thus Vishvamitra started to narrate.

verses.devanagari:
कन्दर्पो मूर्तिमानासीत् काम इत्युच्यते बुधैः |
तपस्यन्तमिह स्थाणुं नियमेन समाहितम्
कृतोद्वाहं तु देवेशं गच्छन्तं समरुद्गणम् |
धर्षयामास दुर्मेधा हुंकृतश्च महात्मना
verses.iast:
kandarpo mūrtimān āsīt kāma iti ucyate budhaiḥ |
tapasyantam iha sthāṇum niyamena samāhitam
kṛta udvāham tu deveśam gacchantam sa marud gaṇam |
dharṣayāmāsa dur.hmedhā hum kṛtaḥ ca mahātmanā
verses.translation: "When Love-god was with his body wise men used to call him Kama, the passion. At this place, that Love-god with his naughty intent braved god of gods Shiva who had been practising ascesis and who concentrated observantly, and who was returning after his marriage along with his followers, namely the Wind-gods, and that great soul Shiva disapprovingly roared at Love-god.
notes: The meaning of kan darpa is one who is carnally, prideful, i.e., he who takes pride in arousing lecherousness. And kāma is 'desire' the natural basic instinct of any animal, and the one which the sages and saints want to overcome, so they named Love-god from their point of view. In these verses the two words kṛta udvāham , and their meaning as on marrying Parvati and going this way with his coterie etc., is held incongruous to other mythological episodes of Shiva's marriage with Parvati, and Manmatha's effort to enkindle love in Shiva. After marriage with Parvati, some argue, where is the question of Love-god's interference to inculcate love in Shiva. It is clear in Rama Charita Maanas how this Shiva-Parvati marriage occurs. And some give the meaning like this: kṛta where kṛ= karaṇe udvāham tu deveśam = to actualise, marriage, only, of Shiva; gacchantam on going there, Love-god, sa marudgaṇam with Wind-gods and other deities; dharṣayāmāsa started to attack Shiva. The Love-god on going there to that hermitage that is being described by Vishvamitra along with Wind-gods et al, with an intention to get the marriage of Shiva performed, assailed Shiva.

glosses.meaning: by wise men, Kama, thus, is called
[disapproving] roar, he made, also - Shiva roared at Love-god.

verses.devanagari:
अवध्यतश्च रौद्रेण चक्षुषा रघुनन्दन |
व्यशीर्यन्त शरीरात् स्वात् सर्वगात्राणि दुर्मतेः
verses.iast:
avadhyataḥ ca rudreṇa cakṣuṣā raghu nandana |
vyaśīryanta śarīrāt svāt sarva gātrāṇi dur.hmateḥ
verses.translation: "And Rama, the wrathful third-eye of Shiva destroyed the lewd-minded Love-god making all his limbs to fall down from his body.
notes: The word avadhyat is otherwise said in other texts as ava dagdhasya rudreṇa cakśusā, to derive a clear meaning of 'burnt down,' because avadhyat is just killing, slaying, whereas Shiva's third-eye truly burns down anything where even ashes do not remain. The critical editions have this as dagdhasya tasya raudreNa chakShuShA

glosses.meaning: with wrathful, eye [third eye,] one who is destroyed

verses.devanagari:
तत्र गात्रं हतं तस्य निर्दग्धस्य महात्मनः |
अशरीरः कृतः कामः क्रोधाद्देवेश्वरेण ह
verses.iast:
tatra gātram hatam tasya nir.hdagdhasya mahātmanaḥ |
aśarīraḥ kṛtaḥ kāmaḥ krodhāt deva Iśvareṇa ha
verses.translation: "There the body of Love-god is evanesced when that great soul Shiva burnt it down, and by the anger of that god of gods Shiva, Love-god is rendered as a bodiless entity.
notes: Manmatha and his wife Rati will have supremely exquisite physiques. At the very sight of Manmatha everybody used to become a prey to lasciviousness. So Shiva had to completely burn down that physical form of love, whereby only kaama, the mental desire, is remaining.

glosses.meaning: by god, of gods - Shiva, by his anger
Love-god, as body less one, made as.

verses.devanagari:
अनङ्ग इति विख्यातस्तदाप्रभृति राघव |
स चाङ्गविषयः श्रीमान् यत्राङ्गं स मुमोच ह
verses.iast:
anañga iti vikhyātaḥ tadā prabhṛti rāghava |
sa ca añga viṣayaḥ śrīmān yatra aṅgam sa mumoca ha
verses.translation: Then onwards Love-god is renowned as Ananga, as he is without body, and where his body is given up that is renowned as Anga province.

verses.devanagari:
तस्यायमाश्रमः पुण्यस्तस्येमे मुनयः पुरा |
शिष्या धर्मपरा वीर तेषां पापं न विद्यते
verses.iast:
tasya ayam āśramaḥ puṇyaḥ tasya ime munayaḥ purā |
śiṣyā dharmaparā vīra teṣām pāpam na vidyate
verses.translation: "This merited hermitage thus belongs to Shiva and, oh, brave Rama, these sages abiding in virtue are Shiva's disciples at one time, thus sin is unverifiable with them.
notes: This hermitage belongs to Love God or Shiva, tasya kāmasya sthāṇorvā. Because Shiva is a god who controls Love-god, kāmesvhvara, this is Shiva's hermitage. The last verse again says it is Kaama's hermitage. And the sages practising ascesis in this hermitage, purā śiṣyā , are the old time disciples of Shiva. pūrva kālam ārabhya...santāna paramparayā śiṣyā. These sages are the progeny of the sages who long time back were the direct disciples of Shiva. Because these are the direct grandchildren of the direct disciples of Shiva, sin cannot touch them. ata eva pāpam teṣāmna vidyate | pūrvam rudra śiṣyā api samprati tat śiṣya kṛtam pāpam navidyate ityarthaḥ || Govindaraja.

glosses.meaning: at one time, his [Shiva's,] disciples, these, sages are

verses.devanagari:
इहाद्य रजनीं राम वसेम शुभदर्शन |
पुण्ययोः सरितोर्मध्ये श्वस्तरिष्यामहे वयम्
verses.iast:
iha adya rajanīm rāma vasema śubha darśana |
puṇyayoḥ saritoḥ madhye śvaḥ tariṣyāmahe vayam
verses.translation: "Let us stay for this night in this hermitage situated in between two meritorious rivers Ganga and Sarayu, oh, Rama with auspicious mien, tomorrow we will cross over the River Ganga.

glosses.meaning: here, meritorious, rivers, in the between of

verses.devanagari:
अभिगच्छामहे सर्वे शुचयः पुण्यमाश्रमम् |
इह वासः परोऽस्माकं सुखं वस्त्यामहे वयम्
स्नाताश्च कृतजप्याश्च हुतहव्या नरोत्तम |
verses.iast:
abhigacchāmahe sarve śucayaḥ puṇyam āśramam |
iha vāsaḥ paro'smākam sukham vastyāmahe vayam
snātāḥ ca kṛta japyāḥ ca huta havyā narottama |
verses.translation: "Let us all purify ourselves by taking our bath, performing our meditations, offering our daily oblations, and then let us enter this meritorious hermitage, thus our stay in here will be comforting to us." So said Vishvamitra to Rama and Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: oh, best one among men, Rama

verses.devanagari:
तेषां संवदतां तत्र तपोदीर्घेण चक्षुषा
विज्ञाय परमप्रीता मुनयो हर्षमागमन् |
अर्घ्यं पाद्यं तथातिथ्यं निवेद्य कुशिकात्मजे
verses.iast:
teṣām saṃvadatām tatra tapo dīrgheṇa cakṣuṣā
vijñāya parama prītā munayo harṣam āgaman |
arghyam pādyam tathā ātithyam nivedya kuśikātmaje
verses.translation: When they are discussing there the sages of that hermitage are highly gladdened to perceive them with their sixth-sense, and on approaching them enchantedly they offered water for hands and feet wash and then offered hospitality firstly to Sage Vishvamitra.

glosses.meaning: asceticism's, by the extent of, [inner] eye [by sixth-sense]

verses.devanagari:
रामलक्ष्मणयोः पश्चादकुर्वन्नतिथिक्रियाम् |
सत्कारं समनुप्राप्य कथाभिरभिरंजयन्
verses.iast:
rāma lakṣmaṇayoḥ paścāt akurvan atithi kriyām |
satkāram sam anuprāpya kathābhiḥ abhirañjayan
verses.translation: Afterwards those sages of that hermitage have accorded reception to Rama and Lakshmana, and applauded by Vishvamitra for their hospitality those sages have entertained Rama and other guests with myths and legends.

verses.devanagari:
यथार्हमजपन् संध्यामृषयस्ते समाहिताः |
तत्र वासिभिरानीता मुनिभिः सुव्रतैः सह
न्यवसन् सुसुखं तत्र कामाश्रमपदे तथा |
verses.iast:
yathā arham ajapan sandhyām ṛṣayaḥ te samāhitāḥ |
tatra vāsibhiḥ ānItā munibhiḥ suvrataiḥ saha
nyavasan susukham tatra kāma āśrama pade tathā |
verses.translation: Those sages with concentrated minds and according to one's own aptitude have meditated upon the deity of sunset when it is sundown, followed by Rama and others. Then led into hermitage by those sages who are with pious commitments and who are dwelling there, Rama and others have very comfortably stayed in the precincts of Shiva's hermitage.

glosses.meaning: deity at sunset - Gayatri, meditated upon
there, who are dwelling [Rama and others]
those [guests] that are led forth [into hermitage]

verses.devanagari:
कथाभिरभिरामभिरभिरामौ नृपात्मजौ | -
रमयामास धर्मात्मा कौशिको मुनिपुङ्गवः
verses.iast:
kathābhirabhirāmabhirabhiramau nṛpātmajau | - yadvā -
kathābhiḥ abhi rāmabhiḥ abhi ramau nṛpa ātmajau
ramayāmāsa dharmātmā kauśiko munipuñgavaḥ
verses.translation: Staying very comfortably in the precincts of Kaama hermitage, then that virtuous sage Vishvamitra, saint the eminent, delighted the delightful princes with delighting stories.....
